description: The first family-F29 arm (DECISIONS.md 9.149): the F28 run stack on a demand where the shared-ride pass may draw its drivers from the whole 25% sample - B.ride.shared_lift_hash_bucket 0.05 -> 0.25, the standing campaign fraction (0.05 = every build before) - and, thinning for the first time on the weekday, binds the LONGEST servable car-less tours first (B.ride.shared_lift_priority = longest_first; `uniform` = before). At 0.05 the bucket rule let each passenger be served by 5% of drivers: 94% of the 27,771 car-less direct tours the pass could not serve had a same-SA2 driver within the window and were refused on the bucket alone, at a median 9-15 km. At the F28 gate car read +6.6% - inside the band for the first time - pairing was solved (0 ride legs without a declared driver, pair rate 0.9965) and the roster live (15,582 drivers waiting for a household car an iteration), yet ride stayed at -42.8%: of 108,629 declared bound trips 56.0% were ridden, and the 20,151 walked instead had a straight-line median of 1.08 km with 65% under 2 km, because the shared pass filled the occupancy volume with a uniform draw whose bound trips have a median of 2.46 km against an observed passenger trip of 9.3-9.8 km. What the arm must answer, in order. (1) PLACEMENT: the share of declared bound trips ridden against 0.560 and the walked-bound median against 1.08 km; ride against -42.8% read TOGETHER with bike (+157.3%), bus (+65.0%) and taxi (+161.1%), whose long car-less trips this placement should draw down. (2) CAR must STAY inside (+6.6% at F28) - the first mode inside a gate; walk against -11.9% and motorbike against +16.1%. (3) The roster and the listener as controls: householdCar waited near 15,582, pair rate near 0.9965, 0 ride legs without a driver. (a) THE ROSTER (9.146): car legs starting with every household car out (0 expected for one-car households), the wait-time distribution, stuck agents attributable to a car that never came back, and where the 29,827 self-driven bound trips settle - onto ride, walk or pt. (b) THE LISTENER: ride legs on persons with no boundDriver (~0 expected) and the pair rate against F26's 0.7865. (c) RIDE against -41.6%, read TOGETHER with car (+11.5%), walk (-22.7%), bike (+118.1%) and taxi (+157.0%): a real ride gain should draw car down and, if the car-less quarter's excess is ride's deficit (9.123), bike and taxi with it; walk left the band the wrong way at F26 as car took its trips, so the seesaw is the thing to watch. (d) The bound-trip selection rate against F26's 0.455 - the selection half of the lane, which is what remains once the second car is gone. (e) The pt SPLIT as a CONTROL: heavy rail +234.7%, bus +40.5%, light rail -55.9%, ferry -70.5% at F26; nothing here touches pt. (f) CONVERGENCE, requirement 8, still unmeasured: innovation off at 240. (g) The awaiting-run measurements the open issues name: #145, #86, #48, #93, #96, #94, #98, #108, #107, #82, #131, #30, #49, #50, #66. S2 x WEEKDAY at 25%, 300 iterations, innovation off at 240, gated every 100 iterations under the loop in GOAL.md with the runner's own watcher stopping the hard bar itself (9.137) - in which case the arm closes itself out as stopped_at_gate and its reading is citable at its reached_iteration and nowhere past it (9.143). 25% is the standing directive (user, 1 Sep). Cost: MEASURED, not projected - the F26 arm took 38,426 s to iteration 100, a mean 384 s an iteration, of which a tenth was milestone output the monitoring never read (9.147); on the F27 stack the three f27_timing_probe_25pct runs read a plain iteration at 264-272 s with the detour routing parallel and RUN.machine.threads = 16, and a milestone now writes a trips table rather than plans and events, so 300 iterations is nearer ~25 h; `wait` adds waiting agents to the qsim and may move that either way, and this arm's own stopwatch is the measurement of both. Graph rendering is OFF (9.59). NEVER compare this arm with any run before the F27 boundary: the demand (householdVehicles, the carve pool), the plans and the compiled controler are all part of a run's identity (9.127, 9.138, 9.142, 9.143, 9.146). NOTHING THIS PRODUCES IS A RESULT until its record says ran_to_last_iteration.
